title: How Does AI-Powered OCR Solve Continuous Ink Jet Printing Challenges?
summary: AI-powered OCR uses pre-trained deep learning neural networks to instantly read faded, smudged, or distorted text on complex packaging surfaces, eliminating the configuration delays and high false-reject rates of traditional rule-based OCR.

# How Does AI-Powered OCR Solve Continuous Ink Jet Printing Challenges?


[About the author](https://www.linkedin.com/in/charlie-long-57236023/)


[About the author](https://www.linkedin.com/in/charlie-long-57236023/)

**


AI-powered OCR uses pre-trained deep learning neural networks to instantly read faded, smudged, or distorted text on complex packaging surfaces, eliminating the configuration delays and high false-reject rates of traditional rule-based OCR.


## **Key Takeaways**


The Challenge: Traditional Continuous Inkjet (CIJ) printing and[Optical Character Recognition (OCR)](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/faq/what-is-ocr.html) systems struggle with modern manufacturing demands, including varied packaging surfaces and new regulatory pressures like the FDA’s FSMA 204 rule.


The Solution:[AI-powered OCR](https://www.zebra.com/content/dam/zebra_dam/en/brochure/ebook/machine-vision-deep-learning-ocr-brochure-ebook-en-us.pdf) uses deep learning to accurately read date and lot codes, even when they are smudged, distorted, or printed on reflective or complex materials.


The Advantage: Unlike traditional OCR, which requires extensive training and stable conditions, Zebra's AI OCR is pre-trained and robust, reducing costly downtime, false rejects, and compliance risks.


CIJ is an essential workhorse technology for manufacturers of food and beverages, consumer packaged goods, and cosmetics. A stream of tiny electrically charged ink droplets is transferred onto the surface of a product or packaging, usually depicting a simple alphanumeric like a date or lot code. This process is incredibly high-speed (over 50,000 droplets every second) and works on multiple surfaces and shapes. CIJ has been the gold standard printing methodology for FDA-compliant[manufacturing](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/industry/manufacturing.html) since the Reagan administration and hasn’t evolved much during that time. So, what’s changed?


## Why is Code Inspection Winning on the Manufacturing Margins?


Whether it’s due to greater global competition, rising inflation, or continuously rising consumer expectations, the modern margin game has changed. Efficiency is the new battleground. Who can produce just a little faster? Who can mitigate the most risk or reduce the most waste in their operations? It’s a fight on the fringes, and in this fight, technology and best practices have never mattered more.


## How Does FSMA 204 Rule Impact Traceability?


[Date and lot codes](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/use-case-library/ocr-for-lot-and-date-code-reading-and-verification.html) are a standard part of the manufacturing process and have been for some time. These small lines of text have big responsibilities. They protect consumers and consumer brands from risk and liability. They are a compliance necessity, and they are about to become even more critical with the FDA’s new[FSMA 204 rule](https://www.zebra.com/content/dam/zebra_dam/en/infographic/retail-infographic-fsma-204-en-us.pdf) . This rule adds stringent[traceability](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/industry/manufacturing/use-case/traceability.html) requirements for lot codes for foods that appear on the FDA Food Traceability List. This change will affect some[manufacturers](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/industry/manufacturing/sub-vertical/food-and-beverage-manufacturing.html) more than others, but it puts additional pressure on all to ensure the absolute[verification](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/use-case-library/ocr-label-verification.html) and accuracy of every code, which is impossible using only periodic manual checks.


## New Surfaces and Technologies


Printing accurate dates and lot codes is far from error-proof. Clogged nozzles on a printhead or vibration on the line often result in codes that bleed, smudge, or degrade over time. This issue is further complicated by the fact that packaging has not stood still in the past few decades. Manufacturers are now producing surfaces that are reflective, transparent, glossy, and in an ever-growing variety of shapes and textures.


OCR technology has existed almost as long as CIJ has. Luckily, OCR technology hasn’t stood still, either. AI-powered[machine vision](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/products/industrial-machine-vision-fixed-scanners.html) can recognize and decipher codes that could be distorted or otherwise unrecognizable. And this technology is being harnessed and optimized by Zebra.


## What is the Difference Between AI OCR and Traditional OCR?


Artificially intelligent OCR is changing how manufacturers approach[date and lot code inspection](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/use-case-library/ocr-for-lot-and-date-code-reading-and-verification.html) . Zebra’s AI OCR solution combines industrial imaging hardware,[deep-learning](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/faq/what-is-the-difference-between-machine-learning-deep-Learning.html) software, and line-level integration to capture, read, verify, and act on code data in real time. A[smart camera](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/resource-library/faq/what-is-smart-camera.html) focuses on the region of interest where the code appears and captures an image of that code. Deep learning technology uses software to extract the alphanumeric characters from the image, and the system automatically verifies whether the code is present, readable, and aligned with production requirements.


How is this any different from current OCR technologies? First,[AI OCR smart cameras](https://www.zebra.com/us/en/products/industrial-machine-vision-fixed-scanners/smart-sensors-and-cameras/ns42/ns42.html) don’t need a “perfect” environment to work perfectly. Traditional OCR is notoriously fragile, requiring high-contrast characters and perfect alignment on a flat background to function reliably. Second, traditional OCR systems are not pre-trained. They require significant engineering hours to train and configure the system to recognize different font types and characters; and more hours of costly downtime every time you need to adjust any parameters.


**


# Comparing technologies


Zebra's AI OCR solution offers multiple advantages over traditional OCR systems.


**TRADITIONAL OCR ZEBRA AI OCR**


**Logic** Rule-based template matching Pre-trained neural networks


**Setup and deployment** Tedious: Configuration and training can take 4 hours or more Quick; can be deployed in minutes


**Font flexibility** Fails on new, altered, or stylized fonts Reads more than 200 font families out of the box


**Text legibility** Fails on blurred or distorted text Reads faded, smudged, low-contrast, and highly distorted text


**Surface condition** Fails on textured, reflective, transparent, or other complex surfaces Reads text on paper, plastic, metal, foil, and glass


**Print method** Cannot adapt to changing conditions or print quality Reads continuous inkjet (CIJ), thermal printing, laser marking


**Compute power** Very low; runs on simple CPUs Higher; benefits from more powerful NPUs and GPUs


**


AI OCR doesn’t have either of these drawbacks. It’s designed to work in real-world production lines where motion, vibration, glare, and smudges don’t prevent it from doing its job. It comes pre-trained on more than 200 font families and millions of industrial images so it can be deployed out of the box, already able to reliably decipher any marking method from CIJ to laser, thermal, etched, and dot peen.


## What is the Business Cost of Inaction?


The bottom line is that manufacturers are starting to evaluate the cost-benefit ratio of maintaining the status quo while the situation around them continues to change and evolve. Every false reject, every rejected shipment, every recall, and every minute of rework or downtime has a dollar value. And it all adds up.


In an environment where every process is subject to change, adapting with superior technology is no longer an option. It’s a competitive necessity. By implementing a robust AI-powered OCR solution, manufacturers can protect consumers, ensure compliance, and secure their bottom lines.
